info.title: Lawgraph API
info.description: Lawgraph is a FastAPI layer over the PostgreSQL knowledge graph. It exposes endpoints for articles of law, judgments, parliamentary dossiers and legislative history.

get.description: Looks up an article by `bwb_id` and `article_number`, adds its parent instrument, the number of judgments that cite it (`metadata.judgment_count`; `/cited-by` pages them), and the article references recorded on the article itself; `successors` and `predecessors` give its place in a recodification (`TRANSPOSED_TO`) both ways.

get.summary: Passages of judgments that cite an article
get.description: One row per passage: a judgment and the paragraph in it that cites the article, with the lid, onderdeel or aanhef it names, a snippet and the confidence of the detection. Newest judgment first. `court` (ECLI court code), `tier` and `lid` (a lid number the passage names) filter; `total` counts all passages that match, `judgment_total` the judgments they are in, `echr_judgment_total` the ECHR judgments that cite the article (no passage: HUDOC names the article). 404 when the article is unknown.

get.description: Every version of one article, identified by the stable BWB `stam_id` so renumbering does not break the chain, oldest first, without their text. Each version carries its validity period, the kind of change (`change`: introduces / amends / repeals), the amending publication (`amended_by`) and the commencement publication (`commencement`) with their dossiers, whether its text differs from the version before it (`text_changed`) and which parts it changed (`changes`). The text of a version is at `history/{key}`. An article of a law of the Staatsblad the BWB does not hold has one version: its text as enacted, without a validity, made (`amended_by`) by the publication its text comes from. 404 when the article is unknown.

get.summary: One version of an article with its text
get.description: The version `version_key` (a `key` of `history`) with its text, its parts and tables as spans of the text, and the publications that made it. Two of them side by side are the difference between two versions. 404 when the article is unknown or the version is not one of it.

The dossiers that established (enacted its regulation), introduced, amended or repealed this article, or propose to: one entry per change and dossier, with the publication (enacted, `canoniek`) or the bill (proposed, `voorgesteld`) that carries it; proposed first, then newest first. What only cites the article (a judgment, another article) is not history. The explanatory documents are at `explained-by`. Returns an empty list when there is no history — never a 404.

The documents that explain this article: every EXPLAINS edge that points at the article (`target` `article`) or at one of its versions (`target` `article_version`); an explanation of the law as a whole is no evidence about this article and is not listed. Newest first. An explanation of `scope` `dossier` is written per dossier: the memorandum explains all the changes of the dossier; of `scope` `article` the memorandum names the section about this article in `section_anchor` (the `id` of a section of the document; `GET /api/documents/{key}/passages` gives its text). One document appears once per level. `total` counts all explanations, independent of `limit` and `offset`. Returns an empty list for an unknown article — never a 404.

The papers that explain this article in a passage, each with the text of its passages: the sections `semantic tk-mvt-articles` linked to the article or to one of its versions (of `scope` `article` in `explained-by`). Per paper the version it explains; the newest version first, the article itself (no version) last; of one version the memoranda before the amendments. A section is listed once, with its surest match, in the order of the paper. An explanation of a whole dossier has no passage and is not listed (`explained-by` lists it). Empty for an unknown article — never a 404.

The regulations in force whose preamble ("Gelet op") names this article as their legal basis (`BASED_ON`; a repealed regulation is left out), each with the leden it names and its articles that refer to this one; and the delegation formulas of the article ("bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur"), each with the regulations that fill it, or none yet. 404 when the article is unknown.

A paginated list of judgments with filters on court (the ECLI court code), tier (the Type of the court in the Instanties value list of the Rechtspraak: hoge_raad, raad_van_state, gerechtshof, rechtbank, tuchtcollege, andere_instantie, koninkrijksinstantie, …), court_kind (the kind of court within the tier: ambtenarengerecht, raad_van_beroep, gerecht_in_eerste_aanleg, …), area of law (`subject`), source, date range and a minimum citation count. `facets` counts the judgments under the filters per `tier` (without the tier and court_kind filters), per `court_kind` (without its own filter), per `source` (without the source filter), per year of `date` (without `from` and `to`), per area of law (`subjects`, without `subject`) and per `procedure` (without its filter). `facets=false` leaves them out (null): the pages after the first need none.

paged list, without the judgments known only because something cites them (stubs: no date, court or text) unless `include_stubs=true`, and without a publication of a decision that another publication replaces (`same_as`; `q` its exact ECLI finds it); `q` (a query that is the whole of an ECLI or of a case number, `18/04298`, gives the judgments with it and only those; other text is searched), `court` (ECLI code), `tier` (the `Type` of the court in the Instanties list, one of `core.courts.TIERS`: `hoge_raad`, `raad_van_state`, `centrale_raad_van_beroep`, `college_van_beroep_bedrijfsleven`, `parket` (the conclusions of the Parket bij de Hoge Raad), `gerechtshof`, `rechtbank`, `kantongerecht`, `tuchtcollege`, `andere_instantie`, `koninkrijksinstantie`, `kroon`, `buitenlandse_instantie`, `hvj_eu`, `ehrm`), `court_kind` (the kind of court within the tier, one of `core.courts.COURT_KINDS`: `ambtenarengerecht`, `raad_van_beroep`, `gerecht_in_eerste_aanleg`, …; a tier of one kind of court is its own; see pipelines (docs/pipelines.md#courts)), `source`, `subject` (an area of law, one of `subjects` as written: `Strafrecht`, `Bestuursrecht; Belastingrecht`), `subject_area` (a main area of law, the part of a subject before its first `;`: `Bestuursrecht` holds `Bestuursrecht` and `Bestuursrecht; Belastingrecht` alike), `from`, `to`, `cited_by_min`, `sort` (`date_desc`, `date_asc`, `citation_count`); each item has `tier`, `court_kind`, `subjects` (the areas of law of the source, empty when it gives none), `names` (what lawyers call it, `Haviltex`; empty for most), `decision_kind` (`arrest`, `vonnis`, `beschikking`, `uitspraak`, `conclusie`, `prejudiciële beslissing`, or null; see pipelines (docs/pipelines.md#rechtspraak)), `series_id` and `series_size`, `inbound_citation_count` (the judgments that cite it or a publication `SAME_AS` it) and `outbound_citation_count` (the judgments it cites); `q` also matches `names`. `facets` counts the judgments under the filters, each without its own: `tier` (`value`, `count`, most first; without the `tier` and `court_kind` filters), `court_kind` (the same, without the `court_kind` filter), `source` (`value` `rechtspraak`, `echr`, `cjeu`, `count`, most first; without the `source` filter) `year` (`value` the year of `date`, `count`, oldest first after null, no date; without `from` and `to`), `subjects` (per area of law as written, `Strafrecht`, `Bestuursrecht; Belastingrecht`, most first; a judgment counts for each of its areas; without the `subject` filter), `subject_area` (per main area of law, most first; a judgment counts once for each of its main areas; with `narrower`, the subjects of the source under it, `value` as written for the `subject` filter, `label` the part after its first `;`, `count`; the whole tree without the `subject_area` and `subject` filters) and `procedure` (per Rechtspraak `psi:procedure` as written, `Hoger beroep`, `Cassatie`, null for none, most first; without the `procedure` filter, which filters on that value); the counts of `tier`, `court_kind`, `source` and `year` read an index, not the judgments; the facets and `total` are kept an hour whatever the data does (`db/version_cache.py`), the page itself is read fresh; `facets=false` gives `facets` null and counts nothing but `total`, the choice for the pages after the first

get.summary: One judgment with the articles it cites
get.description:
Looks a judgment up by ECLI, follows its REFERS_TO edges to articles and adds each article with its parent instrument.

the judgment with its `official_url` (uitspraken.rechtspraak.nl by ECLI; HUDOC by item id, `external_id`, for an ECHR judgment; EUR-Lex by CELEX number, `external_id`, for one of a court of the EU; null for a stub of another court), its `paragraphs` (each with a `paragraph_id` for deep links, its printed `number`, its `kind` (`heading`, `subheading`, `body`, `toc`: a line of a table of contents, `signature`: the closing lines that sign a conclusion), of a paragraph without a number that goes on with a numbered consideration `continues` (its `paragraph_id`), and the `citations` in it of an article or a judgment, one per occurrence with `start` and `end`, `kind` `article` or `judgment` and `target.collection` to match; the first is the kop when the judgment has one), its `footnotes` (`label` as printed, `paragraph_id` the paragraph whose marker points to it, null when none does, `at` where that marker stands in the paragraph's `text`, null when not known, `text`, and the `citations` in that text as a paragraph has them), its `parties` (`name`, `role`, `roles` (every role the kop names, in its order: geïntimeerde and appellant in incidenteel hoger beroep), `role_stated` (a derived role is never the other side's for a public authority: the prosecution is `Officier van justitie`), `side` `first`/`second`/`other`, `alias` ("(hierna: X)", and "Partijen worden hierna A, B en C genoemd"), `representatives` (`name`, `role` `advocaat`, `gemachtigde` or, in a criminal case, `raadsman`, `place`, `capacity`: from the kop and the account of the procedure, data model (docs/data-model.md#judgment)); a party the procedure hears "als partij" that the kop does not name comes last, `side` `other`; null when the judgment was normalized before parties were read, empty when none are named), the articles its `REFERS_TO` edges point at with their parent instrument (`articles`), and the same articles as `cited_articles` with the paragraphs that cite them, the lid or onderdeel named and the snippet of the strongest mention: `snippet_paragraph_id` the paragraph it is from (of a citation in a footnote, the paragraph that refers to it, and `footnote` the footnote's `label`; null for a paragraph's own text), `text` the citation as written and `start`/`end` where the linker found it in the snippet (null when the judgment was normalized again since it was linked). Citations are read from the stored edges; nothing is detected per request. `judgment.names` and `decision_kind` as in the list; `summary` is the Dutch inhoudsindicatie and `summary_en` an English one: an English translation (its own ECLI, `translation_of` the ECLI of the Dutch judgment) has the Dutch `summary` of that judgment, and that judgment the English `summary_en` (see data-model (docs/data-model.md#judgment)). `judgment.series_id` and `series_size` name the series of parallel cases it is one of (the same court, day and text), `series` the other judgments of it. `conclusions` are the conclusions its metadata names (`conclusion_eclis`), in that order: `ecli`, `author` (the A-G or P-G), `role` and `date` as the conclusion's light node gives them (`lg_judgment_light`), so they read as the conclusion's own page; one the graph lacks is its `ecli` alone. `cited_judgments` are the judgments its text cites (`REFERS_TO`: by ECLI, LJN or application number), newest first, each with the places that cite it as `cited_articles` has them (`paragraph_ids`, `paragraph_numbers`, `snippet`, `snippet_paragraph_id`, `footnote`, `text`, `start`, `end`, `confidence`, `mention_count`; empty for an edge linked before places were kept); `judgment.same_as` is, for a replaced publication, the ECLI of the one kept (for a language version of an ECHR decision without an ECLI, the HUDOC item id of the version kept), and `same_as` the other publications of the decision (`SAME_AS`, either way); `related_to` the connected cases (`RELATED_TO`, as between dossiers, either way: those its summary names, "Samenhang met 24/03860 E", "Zie ook: ECLI:…", and those whose summary names it), each once with its `links`: per edge its `direction` (`outbound`: this judgment's summary names it, `inbound`: its summary names this one, outbound first), `basis` (`summary_text`) and `text`, the sentence that names it; `judgment.replaced_by` the ECLI `dcterms:isReplacedBy` names, loaded or not. `judgment.advocate_general` and `advocate_general_role` (the role it is signed in: `advocaat-generaal`, `waarnemend advocaat-generaal`, `plaatsvervangend procureur-generaal`, `plaatsvervangend advocaat-generaal`; null when not clear) is, for a conclusion, who wrote it (`T. Hartlief`; null for a judgment); `published_on`, the "Datum publicatie" of uitspraken.rechtspraak.nl (null for another source or without a published document). How it ended (data model (docs/data-model.md#judgment)): `judgment.outcome` (`verworpen`, `vernietigd`, `gedeeltelijk vernietigd`, `vernietigd en verwezen`, `bekrachtigd`, `bevestigd`, `gegrond`, `ongegrond`, `niet-ontvankelijk`, `afgewezen`, `toegewezen`; of the ECHR `schending` or `geen schending`) with `outcome_text`, the clause of the decision that says it ("verwerpt het beroep"), and `outcome_paragraph_id`; of a conclusion `conclusion_outcome` (`verwerping`, `vernietiging`, `vernietiging en verwijzing`, `niet-ontvankelijkverklaring`, `gegrondverklaring`, `ongegrondverklaring`, `beantwoording`) with `conclusion_outcome_text` and `conclusion_outcome_paragraph_id`; of the ECHR `echr_findings`, per article `{article, protocol, combined_with, finding, aspect, text}`; null (empty) when the text does not say it. Each of `conclusions` has the `outcome` and `outcome_text` of that conclusion (what it proposes)

A paginated list of statutes, regulations and EU instruments. Supports free-text search (`q`), a jurisdiction filter (`nl`/`eu`), a kind filter, a minimum article count, and the registers of the BWB: a legal area (`legal_area`, a main area includes its specific areas) and a government theme (`policy_domain`), each by TOOI id or slug; an unknown value finds nothing. `facets` counts the instruments under the filters per legal area (a tree) and per theme, each without its own filter. The regulations that change other regulations (`amending` on an item) are hidden from the list without a search and shown with one; `amending` says otherwise (`hide`, `show`, `only`), and the facet `amending` counts both. The same holds for the instruments no longer in force (`validity`: `in_force`, `expired` or `all`; left out, `in_force` without `q` and `all` with it; `expired_on` on an item, as the BWB gives it, read on the Dutch day). `facets=false` leaves them out (null): the pages after the first need none.

get.description: The instrument named by its BWB id (`BWBR0001854`), its CELEX number (`32016L0680`), the official number of a law of the Staatsblad (`STB-2026-56`: the law, `wet_stb_2026_56`; the publication is `stb_2026_56`) or its node key (`bwbv0001000`, `verdrag_012345`): identifiers, names, jurisdiction, kind, dates and article count, and for a treaty the other instruments with its treaty number (`same_treaty`). 404 for an unknown instrument.

get.summary: The definitions an instrument gives itself
get.description: Its begripsbepalingen, as its text gives them, in the order of the text: each `term` with its `text`, the article and letter it stands in, where it holds (`scope`: the whole regulation, or a chapter or paragraph of it, and whether in the regulations issued under it too) and the regulation a definition is (`refers_to`: `wet`, de Zorgverzekeringswet). Empty for one that defines nothing. 404 for an unknown instrument.

get.summary: EU and international links of an instrument
get.description: `implements`: EU acts this instrument implements; `implemented_by`: the national publications and regulations that implement this EU act. Both are `IMPLEMENTS` edges between instruments with what they rest on (`bases`): EUR-Lex lists the publication as a national implementing measure, or the considerans says so; not per article. `mentions` and `mentioned_by`: the same for an EU act a regulation names by CELEX number without implementing it (`REFERS_TO`). `international`: treaties (BWB treaties) that articles of this instrument refer to, and ECHR judgments that refer to it or to its articles, each with the evidence of its edge; the graph holds no other links to treaties or to the articles of the ECHR Convention from Dutch text. The instrument is named by BWB id, CELEX number or node key; 404 when unknown. `limit` bounds each list; the `*_total` fields are absolute.

The articles in force of this instrument (BWB id or CELEX number), in the order of the document: an article with only a heading (the Algemene bepaling of the Grondwet) where it stands, an annex after the regulation. `include_repealed` adds the repealed identities (last). The text is a short preview; /api/articles/{bwb_id}/{address} has the full content. ``division`` cuts the list to the articles of one division (``total`` and the pages count those), with the division itself in ``division``; 404 when no article stands in it.

Meant for the case-law layer of the graph. ``total`` is the absolute count, independent of ``limit``. ``sort``: ``date`` (default), the newest first; ``cited``, the most cited articles of the law first, then the newest. ``facets.year`` counts every citing judgment per year, not the page; ``year`` keeps the judgments of one year (``total`` and the page).

get.description: Dossiers reached through LEGISLATED_IN from (a) the regulation itself and (b) the amending publications (Stb/Trb) that change, introduce or repeal one of its articles. ``via`` says how the dossier is linked (``instrument`` or ``amending_publication``; in the latter case ``publication`` names the newest publication). ``total`` is the absolute count, independent of ``limit``.

The publications (Staatsblad, Staatscourant, Tractatenblad, ...) that enacted this regulation (ESTABLISHES its articles) or change, introduce or repeal articles of it (AMENDS / INTRODUCES / REPEALS), newest first. Per publication: the edge count per kind, the number of articles affected, the first effective date and the dossiers. ``total`` is the absolute count, independent of ``limit`` and ``offset``. Apart from them, in ``proposals``, the papers of the Tweede Kamer that propose to change it and are pending.

get.summary: Instruments referring to this one, or referred to by it
get.description: The other laws whose articles in force refer to articles in force of this law, or the other way (`REFERS_TO` between articles), the most articles first. Each carries its `kind` and `date_in_force`, the `direction`, the articles at both ends (`outbound_count` articles of this law refer to `outbound_cited_count` of it; `inbound_count` of its articles refer to `inbound_cited_count` of this law) and `basis`: whether one is issued under the other as well (`BASED_ON`), with the articles its preamble names. ``total`` is the absolute count, independent of ``limit``. The articles between the two: `.../references/{other}`.

get.summary: The references between the articles of two instruments
get.description: Every reference (`REFERS_TO`) from an article in force of this instrument to an article in force of `other`, then the other way (`direction` `outbound`, `inbound`), in the order of the referring and the referred article: the `source` and `target` articles, the words of the reference (`text`), the parts of the target it names and its `semantic_type`. Both are a BWB id or a CELEX number; empty for an unknown one or the same one twice.

The regulations in force whose preamble ("Gelet op") names an article in force of this law as their legal basis (`BASED_ON`), one per regulation with the articles it names, whether those give the power it is made under (`basis_kind`), its articles that work each out (`referring`), the other laws it names (`also_based_on`) and the regulations issued under it in turn (`sub_delegated`): AMvBs first, then ministerial regulations, then the others; by title. A repealed regulation (as on the list: `expired_on` today or before) or article is left out. Empty for an unknown instrument.

get.summary: The laws a regulation is issued under

get.summary: Explore a node and its neighbors
get.description:
Fetches a node from the given collection and returns its neighbors from the unified edge collection in buckets, one per relation, direction and neighbor collection. Each neighbor carries the edge that leads to it: `edge_id`, `status`, `confidence` and `meta`. A bucket holds one page (`limit` neighbors from `offset`, in the same order on every request), its `total`, and the `next_offset` of the following page (null on the last). `relations`, `node_types`, `direction` and `status` narrow the edges; the totals count what remains.

a node (any node collection) with its neighbours in buckets of one relation, direction and neighbour collection, a page of `limit` (at most 200; 500 with `props=canvas`) from `offset` in each. An article's `lid_counts` are waited for only on the first page with every prop: a further page or a page of the canvas gives those counted before, or none while they are being counted. Every neighbour carries its edge: `edge_id` (the edge `key`), `status`, `confidence`, `meta`. The node, every neighbour and every node of a neighbourhood or path has `title`, the `<title>` of its page (`core.names.title_of`; of a publication with the title of its nota van toelichting; with `props=canvas` too, which keeps what it reads), and a judgment `cite` (as on `/api/judgments/{ecli}`); a dossier has in its props `short_title` and `short_title_basis` as the feed gives them, a decision `short_subject` (the name what was voted on goes by: `Wet AI-toezicht`, `Begroting Defensie 2027`; null without one), a paper or a case `kind_group`. `props=canvas` gives a neighbour only what the canvas of the explorer draws: of its props those of its collection and those its title reads (`_rows.canvas_keys`; of each of its `actors` the role, name and faction; an instrument its `kind` (`wet`, as `/api/instruments/{identifier}` gives it), an annex its `label` and `title`, an instrument version the citation title of its law, `instrument_citation_title`, from the columns of `instruments`; a motion, an amendment or a judgment its `outcome` alone of how it ended), of its edge's `meta` the keys the canvas reads (null when none, never `{}`); the node itself stays whole. A bucket has `type`, `total` (its edges), `next_offset` (null on the last page), `lid_counts`, `capacity_counts` and `items`; `capacity_counts`, of a member's `AUTHORED` (outbound): per capacity they signed in (`meta.capacity`: `kamerlid`, `bewindspersoon`, `overig`; `""` for none), how many of the whole bucket and not only of its page (`{"kamerlid": 980, "bewindspersoon": 503}`), from `lg_authored`; null for every other bucket and with a `status` filter; `lid_counts`, of an article: per lid the edges of the whole bucket cite (in their `meta`: `lid`, `leden`, and the `leden` of each of a judgment's `mentions`), how many do (only the leden the article has: a citation can give it the lid of another article it names), `""` for those that cite none and an edge that cites two counted for each (`{"1": 28, "2": 174, "": 12}`); with `limit=1` (the light node) an article whose lid counts are not kept yet waits for them 0.5 s at most, then answers with every `lid_counts` null and `lid_counts_pending` true while they are counted (a larger `limit` waits for them), so that a reader can show them without reading every page (counted over the meta of every edge of the article, so kept an hour whatever the data does, a newer count made in the background after that; those of the 20 most cited articles warmed); null for a bucket that cites no lid and for a node that is no article; `limit` (default 30, max 200) and `offset` page inside every bucket. Bucket and page order are the same on every request. A neighbour is light: its `props` leave out besides those the text of a paper (`sections`, `footnotes`), the structure of an article (`parts`, `references`, `breadcrumb`) and the rollups of an activity (`case_ids`, `case_kinds_by_dossier`; the node itself keeps them); a judgment carries `ecli`, `display_name`, `names`, `summary`, `date`, `court`, `court_code`, `case_number`, `source`, `stub`, `translation_of`, `advocate_general`, `advocate_general_role`, `outcome`, `outcome_text`, `conclusion_outcome`, `conclusion_outcome_text` and `echr_findings` alone (`lg_judgment_light`), and its `tier` (`hoge_raad`, `hvj_eu`, `ehrm`: by its court code, of code XX by the court it names) and its `source` (by its ECLI) where those lack them; its `summary` is cut at 400 characters (with `…`), and the `meta` of its edge leaves out `mentions` (each place a judgment cites the article or the judgment; `/api/judgments/{ecli}` has them), which the node itself, `/api/documents/{key}` and `/api/articles/...` carry. The answer has the `title` and `description` of the node's page (as `/render` gives them, from the node's own props: without the outcome of a motion or the counts of an article; `title` is the page's `<title>` without `, Concordans`, never cut, the title the app's tab shows: `Art. 6:162 BW, Onrechtmatige daad` (an article with its heading, else its `caption`), `Motie 36496-71 Bolhuis over een AI-killswitch` (a motion or an amendment by its number, then every word of its subject), `HR 20 december 2019 (Urgenda), ECLI:NL:HR:2019:2006`, `36600-VII Begroting Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties 2025`; a day in a title or a description as `20 december 2019`) and its readable `path` (null for a node without one, an activity). The `meta` of a neighbour's edge holds `paragraphs` where a judgment cites: the numbers of the paragraphs it cites in ("4.3", as the judgment prints them), stored on an edge to a cited judgment and taken from the mentions of an edge to a cited article, so a list of citing judgments shows where each cites without a request per row. With `edge_meta=passages` (also with `props=canvas`) it holds `passages` too, from the mentions of the edge: the first place in each of its first three paragraphs (a footnote counts apart), each `paragraph_id`, `paragraph_number`, `footnote` (its label, null in the paragraph itself), `snippet`, `text` (the citation as written) and `start`, `end` (`snippet[start:end]` is `text`), so a row or a card shows the passage without the judgment; none of a mention linked before it kept `snippet_start`. `light` (the default) leaves them out: they weigh about 0.9 kB an edge. The `meta` of an edge from a Tweede Kamer paper holds `place`, where its citation stands in what `/api/documents/{key}` serves (`part` `title`, `text` with `section_id`, or `footnote` with `footnote_id`; `start` and `end` in that part; see data-model (docs/data-model.md#judgment))

get.summary: Resolve a citation, identifier or law name to one node
get.description:
Reads `q` as a citation (`art. 6:162 BW`, `artikel 287 Sr`, `Sr 287`), an identifier (ECLI, BWB id, CELEX id), a Kamerstuk (`36327`, `36327-3`, `Kamerstukken II 2020/21, 36327, nr. 3`) or the name of a law, and answers with the one best match (`id`, `key`, `collection`) and up to five alternatives. A citation that leaves the book of the Burgerlijk Wetboek open (`art. 3 BW`) has no match: its alternatives are the article in every book, in book order. `confidence` says how sure the match is. Nothing that fits answers 200 with kind `none` and no match: the query is then words for `/api/search`.

the one node a citation, identifier or law name names (an article also without the word artikel, law first or number first: `Sr 287`, `6:162 BW`, `287 Sr`; a paper by its number in the Tweede Kamer, `Kamerstukken II 2025/26, 36799, nr. 3`, or by its letter in the Eerste Kamer, `Kamerstukken I 2025/26, 36799, A`; a number right behind the dossier number and a hyphen is the subdossier with that suffix when there is one (`21501-31`), else the paper (`36799-3`); a publication, `Staatsblad 2026, 94`, `Stb. 2026, 94`, `Stcrt. 2026, nr. 12345` or `Trb. 2018, 201`, as the `instrument` it is): `kind` (`article`, `instrument`, `judgment`, `dossier`, `document`, `commitment`, `faction`, `member`, or `none`), `match` (`id`, `key`, `collection`, `kind`, `display_name`, `title` as `/api/nodes` gives it, `confidence`), `confidence`, `alternatives` (up to five, same shape, best first; an article, also a stub without a name of its own, named as it is cited: `Art. 7:162 BW`), `alternatives_total` (how many alternatives were found), `qualifier` (`derde lid` of `artikel 287, derde lid, Sr`) and `notation`, the notation `q` is (`kind` and its `parts`), with a match or without one (`TZ202603-130` that names no commitment of the graph), null for words. A query that is the whole abbreviation, name or alias of a faction, or the whole name of a member, any case and without accents, is that faction or member (`VVD`, `dilan yesilgoz-zegerius`; confidence 0.9; of several factions the seated one, then the most seats), before a law of the same name, which is then an alternative (`VVD` is also the abbreviation of the Warenwetregeling Vrijstelling vitamine D). A citation of the Burgerlijk Wetboek that leaves the book open (`art. 3 BW`, `3 BW`, `artikel 162 BW`) is a choice: `kind` `article`, `match` null, `confidence` 0.5 and as `alternatives` the article of that number in every book that has one, the most cited first, of as many in the order of the books (`artikel 162 BW`: Boek 6 first; up to ten), the `qualifier` for each; one book that has it is the match. A book and a number without a law (`art. 6:162`) is that article of the book, or of a law whose own number it is (`art. 8:69`: the Awb's 8:69 and Boek 8 BW article 69, a choice, the most cited first); `boek 6 art 162` is article 162 of book 6. Nothing that fits is 200 with `kind` `none` and `match` null, so the caller searches the words instead; only an empty or over-long `q` is 422

get.description:
Searches articles, judgments, dossiers and documents. Use `types` to restrict the search to specific collections and `kind` to facet on document or dossier kinds. Every hit has a `score` between 0 and 1, its rank tier for the query: the query is an identifier of the hit (1), its whole name (0.75), the start of its name (0.5), part of its name (0.25) or the hit matched on words only (0.1). Hits of a type come best score first. With `resolve=true` the answer also holds `resolved`, what `/api/resolve` answers for `q`: one request for a search box that goes to the node a citation names and lists the hits otherwise.

text search over `types` (`articles`, `cabinets`, `commitments`, `committees`, `decisions`, `documents`, `dossiers`, `factions`, `instruments`, `judgments`, `members`; all by default), `kind`, `limit`, and a period `from`, `to` (YYYY-MM-DD, both days in it, either open; 422 for `from` after `to`): each hit by a date of its own, in full and live search alike: a judgment the day of its decision (`date_eff`), a paper its date, a dossier the day it was opened, a vote its date, a commitment the day it was made, a law the day it came into force (`date_in_force`), an article the day its law came into force; a type without a date of its own (a member, a faction, a committee, a cabinet) finds nothing within a period. A citation in `q` (`art. 6:162 BW`, `artikel 287 Sr`, `Sr 287`, a full ECLI) puts its article or judgment first, and so does the whole name of a judgment (`Urgenda`, `Lindenbaum/Cohen`: one of its `names`, any case). Every hit has a `score`, its rank tier for `q`: an identifier of the hit (1), its whole name (0.75), the start of its name (0.5), every word of `q` in its name (0.25), a match on words only (0.1), compared in lower case and without accents (`yesilgoz` is part of `Yeşilgöz-Zegerius`); a type lists its hits best first, ties in database order. The names of a hit are its `display_name`, citation title, the `heading` of an article and the `aliases` of an instrument (`BW`, `Boek 6 BW`, `6 BW`: 0.75, before the words); `q` inside the title of a division an article stands in counts as part of its name (0.25). Scores compare across types: a heading or alias that is `q` (0.75) outranks a judgment that only holds its words (0.1). A word of `q` also finds its plural or singular where the last consonant changes between them, which stem apart (`huurprijs` and `huurprijzen`, `brief` and `brieven`). Within a type the database orders by BM25 before the `limit` (on a large table its statistics, the number of rows and the mean length of a field, are an estimate from a fixed sample, at most 6 hours old; the number of rows that hold a common word is the planner's estimate from its statistics, a rare word is counted, and a count that takes over 5 s weighs its terms as held by every row; a word matches the start of a value or a part of it from three characters, the start in any case and, in a name or title, without accents), with a word in a heading (x4), a division title (x1.5), a display name (x2), an alias or short title (x3) weighing more than one in a text; an instrument whose alias or short title is the whole of `q` is always fetched. An article is also found by its terms, what the judgments that cite it call it (`noodweer`: art. 41 Sr, whose words do not hold it; `lg_article_terms`), as a match on words (0.1), ranked above those that only hold the word; such a hit has `extra.terms`, the words of `q` it was found by, which come from the case law, not from the law. An article of which every word of `q` is a strong term (a good share of the judgments that use the word cite it, and few judgments cite it at all: `verjaring`, art. 3:310 BW) scores as a whole name (0.75), the best by its words first. A word of `q` that is the short title or an alias of a law (as the instrument has it, whole, any case and without accents: `Cbw`, `Sr`, `BW` of every book) also matches each of its articles, as the name of the law in its `display_name` does (`zorgplicht cbw`: art. 21 of the Cyberbeveiligingswet), and each dossier the law is `LEGISLATED_IN` (`cbw`: dossier 36764, the bill that became it; ranked above a dossier that only holds the word), in full and live search alike. `dossier` and `dossiers` name the type and are left out of a search of dossiers unless they are all of `q` (`cbw dossier` asks for the dossier of the Cbw). `extra` of an article carries `instrument_title` (its law), `instrument_abbreviation`, `heading` and `division_titles` (its `display_name` the article as it is cited: `Art. 6:162 BW`), of an instrument `short_title`, `aliases`, `kind` and the dates `date_published`, `date_in_force` and `version_date_in_force` (as `/api/instruments/{identifier}` gives them; regulations of one title told apart by them), of a judgment `ecli`, `appno`, `names` and `cite` (as `/api/judgments` gives it; and `person` when it was found by one), of a document `dossier_number`, of a dossier `number`, `kind`, `current_phase`, `closed`, `outcome` and `short_title` (the name it goes by, as `/api/dossiers` gives it: `Wet betaalbare huur`; null without one). A judgment is also found by a person it names (`lg_judgment_persons`: a party not anonymised, whoever acts for a party) when every word of `q` is a word of that one name, whole (while typing, `mode=live`, the last word by its start): `R. van Gelder`, `Van Gelder` and `mr. drs. R. van Gelder` find `mr. drs. R. van Gelder`, `Vermeulen` finds `mr. I.T.F. Vermeulen`, `college van gedeputeerde staten van Zuid-Holland` finds that party; at least one word of three characters or more that is no title, article or particle (`van`, `mr`); the newest first of the first 2,000 names found. Such a hit has `extra.person` (`name` as written, `role`: the party's role, or `advocaat`, `gemachtigde`, `raadsman` of who acts for one, and `party`: the alias or name of the party they act for, null for a party) and scores 0.25 when `q` is all of the name but its titles, initials, articles and particles, else 0.1 after the judgments found by their words. A member is found by every word of its names (its name, party and the factions of its timeline), a faction by its name, abbreviation and aliases; a word without accents or in capitals finds a name with them (`yesilgoz`: Yeşilgöz; of a member in its own name only; a member without a role, `extra.has_role` false, after every member with one, whatever its score). A cabinet is found by every word of its name (`Rutte`, `kabinet Schoof`), newest first, with `from_date` and `to_date` in `extra`; a commitment by every word of its text or its number (`TZ202609-011`), newest first, with `number`, `made_on`, `status`, `minister_name`, `cabinet` and `ministry` in `extra`. A vote (`decisions`) by every word of what was voted on (`subject`) or its `kind` (`Motie`, `Wetgeving`), newest first, with `date`, `kind`, `passed`, `chamber` and `dossier_numbers` in `extra`; `stemming`, `stemmingen`, `besluit` and `besluiten` name the type and are left out (`stemming abortus` asks for the votes on abortion). A document hit has in `extra` its `kind`, `external_id`, `dossier_number`, `sequence` (its number in the dossier: nr. 12), `number` (as above: `12`, the letter `A` of an Eerste Kamer paper), `date` (as the source gives it; null when it has none), `chamber` (`TK`, `EK`, null for Staatsblad and Staatscourant, as in `/api/documents`) and `dossier_short_title` (the name its dossier goes by, as `/api/dossiers` gives it; null without one); with `resolve=true` also `resolved`, what `/api/resolve` answers for `q` (kind `none` for a query over 200 characters), null without it: a search box resolves and searches in one request. `mode=live` (while typing; `full` is the default) answers all types within 250 ms together (a type that waited for a thread has what is left): a type not done by then is empty and named in `partial` (`{"judgments": true}`; a type not cut off is not in it); nothing is ranked by its words (no BM25): each word of `q` is a word of a field (every word it holds: `20/325` both 20 and 325), a whole value (a number, an identifier) or, from three characters, the start of a word of a name or title (`stik`: Stikstofwet; not `tikst`, which the full search finds), and of the first 2,000 rows found those whose name or title starts with `q` come first, then the most cited articles, the laws with the most articles, the dossiers with the latest activity and the newest papers; the judgments are found without ranking their summaries: by ECLI, by a part of a name (`Urgenda`), or by every word of three characters or more in the display name (court, date, case number), the most cited first, and when none does (a subject, `onrechtmatige daad`) the newest that hold the words (summary, name, display name; of the first 2,000 found, without a rank); a query of fewer than three characters finds no judgment. The full search ranks each type within 3 s: a type that takes longer answers what its live search finds (within 1 s more; for judgments that no name or display name holds: the newest that hold the words, of the first 2,000 found, without a rank) and is named in `partial` too, instead of the request answering 503 at its deadline; the next search of the same terms finds what it counted meanwhile

get.description:
Document counts per collection without stubs, the stubs per collection (nodes known only because something refers to them), the replaced publications of a decision (`replaced`) and edge counts per relation type. `nodes.judgments` counts a decision once, as `/api/judgments` does.

`nodes`: document count without stubs of `instruments` (without the publications), `publications` (the Staatsblad, Staatscourant and Tractatenblad publications), `articles`, `judgments`, `documents`, `cases`, `dossiers`, `activities`, `decisions`, `commitments`, `committees`, `members` and `cabinets` (not `factions`, `annexes`, `instrument_versions` or `article_versions`); `stubs`: per collection that has them (`instruments`, `articles`, `judgments`) the nodes known only because something refers to them; `replaced`: per collection that has them (`judgments`) the publications of a decision another loaded publication replaces (`SAME_AS`), which `nodes.judgments` leaves out as `/api/judgments` does, so it equals the `total` of that list; `edges`: `total` and `by_relation`; `by_source`: `judgments` and `documents` per `props.source`; `instruments`: `by_kind` and `by_jurisdiction` (publications included); `data_as_of`: per source (`tk`, `eerstekamer`, `rechtspraak`, `staatsblad`, `staatscourant`, `bwb`, `eurlex`, …) `retrieved_at` (when its newest raw record was fetched) and `newest` (the date of its newest dated record on or before today: a paper, a judgment, a publication, a version coming into force; null for a source without dated records), read at most once a minute; `lists`: per list the `total` its endpoint gives without a filter (its first page), so a count next to a list equals the list: `instruments`, `judgments`, `dossiers`, `documents`, `members`, `bewindspersonen` (`/api/members?government=true`), `factions`, `committees`, `cabinets` and `commitments` (the length of the list for those without `total`), each kept until its tables change, and `decisions` as the list opens (`chamber=TK`) from the count that list keeps, never waited for: null while it is counted (after a change of the decisions, until the warm-up or a visitor of the list has counted it), which a front end shows as nothing, not 0

The judgments whose text is loaded, per court tier and per court, with the date of the oldest and the newest of each; and how many judgments are known only because a loaded one cites them (`stubs`). A decision published twice counts once, as in `/api/judgments`: `replaced` counts the publications another loaded one replaces. A count of judgments anywhere in the API (the judgments that cite an article, for one) is a count of this selection, not of the case law.

A page of decisions — one per Besluit — newest first, optionally filtered by kind, outcome, party (and how it voted), chamber, dossier, date and subject. ``total`` is the absolute count, independent of ``limit``. ``facets`` counts the decisions under the filters: per ``kind`` (without the kind filter; with how many carried and did not), per outcome ``passed`` (without the passed filter), per day and per year (under all filters), and with ``party_votes`` how the factions asked voted on them. ``facets=false`` gives null for ``total`` and ``facets`` and counts nothing: the pages after the first need neither.

decisions with every vote cast — per member on a roll-call, per faction otherwise; the decided motion, amendment or bill with text. The list filters on `kind` (comma-separated: the `Zaak.Soort` of the case decided as the Kamer writes it, `Motie`, `Amendement`, `Wetgeving`, `Begroting`, …; see data model (docs/data-model.md)), `passed`, `party` (the decisions its faction voted on; with `vote` `voor`/`tegen` the ones it voted that way on; a roll-call has no faction vote), `chamber` `TK`/`EK` (the votes of the Eerste Kamer: a decision per vote of its list, with `result` `Aangenomen`/`Verworpen` as it shows it, `method` as its report names it, `bill_decision` (whether it is the vote that decided the bill: the list names a vote on a motion by its bill too), `kind` (of the vote that decided the bill: the kind of its dossier, `Wetgeving`, …; null for a vote on a motion, which the list names no kind of), and in the detail `factions_for`, `factions_against`, `factions_noted`, `bill_url`, `source_url`, `retrieved_on`; no votes per faction, so no `tally`), `dossier` number, `from` and `to` (the date of the vote, YYYY-MM-DD) and `q` (words of the subject, in any case, as the feed matches them: each from the start of a word, one of at most four characters as a whole word: `ai` finds AI-modellen, not AIV or universitaire; `algoritme` algoritmes, not rekenalgoritme; repeated, any of them: `q=AI&q=kunstmatige intelligentie`, each decision once). The list holds the decisions with an outcome (`passed` set), and its facets count those; `unvoted=true` also those that never came to a vote: a motion or amendment withdrawn, postponed, held or lapsed (`decision_kind` `Stemmen - ingetrokken`, `- uitstellen`, `- aangehouden`, `- vervallen`), `passed` null. Each item has `kind` and `decision_kind` (the `BesluitSoort`: `Stemmen - aangenomen`, `Stemmen - zonder stemming aannemen` for a hamerstuk without votes, `Stemmen - uitstellen`, whose `passed` is null); `total` is the matches, independent of `limit`. `facets` counts the decisions under the filters: `kind` (`value`, `count`, how many `passed` and `rejected` (the rest have no outcome), most first; without the `kind` filter), `passed` (`value` `true`/`false`/null, `count`; without the `passed` filter), `days` (`date`, `count`, how many `passed`, oldest first) and `years` (`year`, `count`, `passed`, `rejected`, oldest first) under every filter, and `party_votes`: with `party_votes` (comma-separated faction keys, or `all` for every faction that voted on one of them; it keeps no decision out, unlike `party`), per faction by key (`party`, `name` its abbreviation) how it voted on the decisions under every filter, `voor`, `tegen` and `none` (another choice, or no vote of the faction: a roll-call vote is one of members), in all, per `kind` and per `years`; `[]` without it. They are counted on demand and kept an hour under each filter, whatever the data does; a request waits for them 3 s at most, then the page comes with `[]` and `partial` true, and a request after the count has them. The page is read first and alone (in the order of the list, as far as it goes: `decisions_list_date`); `total` and the other facets are counted per filter and kept until the decisions change (an hour at most): a request waits for them 3 s at most, then the page comes whole with `total` null, empty facets and `partial` true, and a request after the count has them (the lists the explorer opens, of both Kamers and of the Tweede Kamer, are counted in the warm-up); `facets=false` gives null for `total` and `facets` and counts nothing (not `party_votes` either), the choice for the pages after the first. An item has `display_name` (the heading of the vote, distinct per motion on one agenda item: `Motie 2024Z17945: …`); list and detail have `primary_case_kind`, `dossier_numbers` and `chamber` A vote on a motion has `dictum`, what the motion asks or says as it writes it (from `verzoekt`, `roept … op`, `spreekt uit`, `draagt … op` or `vraagt` to `en gaat over tot de orde van de dag`), in the list and the detail; null for any other vote and for a motion without text. List and detail have `motion` (`collection`, `key`, `path`), the motion or amendment the vote was taken on: the oldest paper of the case the vote singled out (`primary_case_kind` `Motie` or `Amendement`; the paper `/{key}/document` and the dictum come from), else, for a vote whose `kind` is one, the Kamerstuk it is `ABOUT` (a vote of the Eerste Kamer on a motion); null for any other vote and for a case without a paper. The detail has `primary_document` (`id`, `key`, `kind`, `title`, `number`, `dossier_number`, `date`, `path`), the Kamerstuk the vote was taken on as `/{key}/document` finds it (of the case it singled out, then of its other cases, the oldest paper; else the Kamerstuk it is `ABOUT`): the motion, the amendment or the bill; null without one. A vote of the Tweede Kamer under a cabinet carries `coalition` (on the list and the detail; `semantic tk-coalition-votes`): the `cabinet`, the seats `coalition_for`, `coalition_against`, `opposition_for`, `opposition_against` (a faction with its seats that day, a member of a roll call as one), `pattern` (`together`, `split`, `wissel`: split, and the side with the most coalition seats lost, a wisselmeerderheid), `carried` (passed with the coalition's seats alone more than half cast) and `decisive` (the opposition alone would have decided otherwise); null without a cabinet or a coalition vote and in the Eerste Kamer. `coalition=together|split|wissel|carried|decisive` filters on it, and `facets.coalition` counts each under every filter but its own; `facets.coalition_cabinets` gives per cabinet (`cabinet`, `name`, newest first) under every filter, a topic of the Overzicht being its words, Kamer and period, its `votes` and how many were `together`, `split`, `wissel`, `carried` and `decisive`

get.description:
The seated parties with their seat counts, in the order they sit in the plenary hall from the chair's left (the plan of the Tweede Kamer, kept with `lawgraph curated set seating`; a faction it does not place sits at the right end) — enough to render a hemicycle. `seating_plan` names the plan. With `date`, the seats on that day: those the members held (FractieZetelPersoon, every seat from the Kamer installed on 30 November 2006; before it only the seats of members who also sat later), in the order of today's plan.

seated factions with seat counts in the order they sit in the plenary hall, from the chair's left (`order`), after the seating plan of the Tweede Kamer (`seating_plan`: `title`, `dated`, `url`, `page`; kept with `lawgraph curated set seating`, updated at every Presidium decision on the seating; a faction the plan does not place sits at the right end); `?date=YYYY-MM-DD` gives the seats the members held that day (complete from the Kamer installed on 30 November 2006) and per faction its `vacant` seats that day, no member holding them (with `seats`, the faction's seats as the stretches of `/api/cabinets/{key}/seats` count them), in the order of today's plan. `?chamber=EK`: the seats of the Eerste Kamer (`total_seats` 75) as eerstekamer.nl shows them on the day it was last read (`as_of`, `source`), in the order of their size, no `seating_plan`; with `date`, the seats of that day as walked from the Kiesraad's result through the changes the Kamer's pages tell (`normalize eerstekamer-mutations`; `source.composition_date` the first day of that stretch, `checked` false when its term did not add up, a faction of the past with `id` and `key` null; `hall` from `hall_read_on` on; 404 before 2003). Each faction has `colors`, the colours that Kamer draws it in (two for a faction drawn in stripes, PRO in the Tweede Kamer; empty for none), and `color`, the first of them or else the party's house colour. Each faction has `coalition` (of the coalition of the cabinet in office on `as_of`, named in `cabinet`: `key`, `name`; null when none was), so the hall can mark coalition and opposition

get.description:
What was promised and proposed, as a stream of events, newest first: ``toezegging`` (a commitment made), ``Voorstel van wet``, ``Nota van wijziging``, ``Amendement``, ``Motie`` and ``Brief regering`` (a Tweede Kamer paper submitted, by its ``Document.Soort`` before `` (``), ``stemming`` (a vote with its outcome), ``publicatie`` (in the Staatsblad, Staatscourant or Tractatenblad) and ``inwerkingtreding`` (a new version of a law in force) and ``uitspraak`` (a judgment or conclusion, on the day it was published; only with ``kind=uitspraak`` or ``tier``, of the highest courts and the Parket unless ``tier`` asks for others). Ordered by date, then by ``id``, both descending; ``next_cursor`` gives the next page, which neither repeats nor skips an event. ``facets`` counts per ``kind``, ``ministry``, ``faction`` and ``cabinet`` the events under the other filters, with ``total``; ``facets=false`` leaves both out and reads only one page.

`items`, `next_cursor`, `total`, `facets`, `partial`, `searched_from` and `data_as_of` (as in `/api/stats`). `total` and `facets` are counted from `lg_feed_events` (`/api/feed/periods`; as `lawgraph feed-events` last wrote it: the last 14 days after every poll, every event each night), by its indexes, each facet as the feed counts it, and kept an hour; under `member`, `tier` or `instrument`, or before that table is ever written, over every event under the filters itself. A request waits for them 3 s at most: under filters not counted before (cold, a minute or more on the full graph) the page comes at once with both null and `partial` true, and a request after the count has them. Filters: `kind` (comma-separated), `since`, `until` (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive), `cabinet` (a key: the events from its beëdiging to that of the next cabinet), `ministry`, `dossier` (the start of a dossier label: `36600` holds `36600-VII`, `37020-` the chapters), `member` (a member key: the papers they signed, the votes on them, the commitments they made), `faction` (a faction key: the papers its Kamerleden signed for it and the votes on them; without `since` its page is read as under `q`), `q` (words of the title or of the title of the event's dossier, or of a publication the names of the laws it changes or enacts and the official title of a law it enacts (from `lg_feed_events`: a publication is found by them once `lawgraph feed-events` wrote it), any case; each word from the start of a word, one of at most four characters as a whole word (`ai`: the AI-verordening, not universitaire; `stikstof`: Stikstofbank, not natuurstikstof; repeated, at most ten times, any of them: `q=AI&q=kunstmatige intelligentie`, each event once); each kind finds them by index where it can (from three characters); without `since` the page is read once from the first day it reaches back to, the day of the (`limit` + 1)-th newest matching event in `lg_feed_events` (`/api/feed/periods`; no later than 14 days ago, what that table may still lack, nor than the day of the cursor), when that table is written and the filters are ones it keeps; else, or when that read finds less than the table counted, the events are searched back from `until`, the cursor or today in windows of 90 days, a year, three years and then the rest, newest first, until the page is full or 8 s are spent: then the page has what was found, `partial` true and `searched_from`, the first day searched, and a request with `until` the day before goes on; `searched_from` is null when every day was searched), `tier` (comma-separated tiers as in `/api/judgments`: keeps judgments alone, of those tiers; without it the feed's judgments are of the default tiers), `chamber` (`EK`: the votes of the Eerste Kamer, only the one that decided each bill; `TK`: the papers, votes and commitments of the Tweede Kamer; publications and commencements are of neither), `coalition` (what the coalition did on a vote of the Tweede Kamer, as `vote.coalition` says it: `together`, `split` (on both sides, a wisselmeerderheid too), `wissel`, `decisive`; keeps votes alone), `instrument` (a BWB id: the events tied to that law: the publications that enact it or change it or its articles, the papers that propose to (a `voorgesteld` change), the events of the dossiers it or such a publication was `LEGISLATED_IN` and of the dossiers of those papers, its new versions and those of the regulations `BASED_ON` it, the judgments that cite it; without `since` read as under `q`, in windows; its total and facets are counted from the events themselves), `article` (with `instrument`, an article number of that law, `3:2`: the events tied to that article, the versions of the law that changed it, the dossiers of the publications and papers that change it, not those of the law itself nor its enactment; 422 without `instrument`); `limit` (1-200, default 50), `cursor` (the `next_cursor` of the page before; 422 for a token the API did not hand out). Order: `date`, newest first; within a day by kind, in the order `Voorstel van wet`, `stemming`, `toezegging`, `inwerkingtreding`, `publicatie`, `Nota van wijziging`, `Amendement`, `Motie`, `Brief regering`; within a kind by `id`. The cursor holds the date, kind and id of the last event of its page, and a page starts after it, so pages neither repeat nor skip an event. `facets` (default true) counts per `kind`, `ministry`, `faction`, `cabinet`, `chamber` (`TK`, `EK`, null for a publication or a commencement) and `coalition` (the values of the filter; a vote counts for each that holds, `split` with every `wissel`, an event without a coalition vote for none) (`{value, count}`, the largest first, `value` null for none) the events under the other filters, and `total` under all of them, whatever the cursor; `facets=false` gives null for both and reads one page only, the choice for the pages after the first. Each item says what it is tied to, read for the items of the page alone: `matched` (with `q`, per word the event holds `{term, field}`, `term` as it was asked and `field` the first of `title` (its own title, of a bill not that of its dossier), `dossier_title` (the whole title of its first dossier) and `laws` (of a publication, the names of its laws) that holds it; empty without `q`), `via` (with `instrument`, how the event is tied to the law: `relation` `establishes`, `amends`, `introduces` or `repeals` (a publication), `proposes` (a paper with a `voorgesteld` change of it, or an event of the dossier of such a paper), `version_of` (a new version of the law), `based_on` (of a regulation issued under it), `refers_to` (a judgment), `legislated_in` (an event of a dossier the law or a publication of it was legislated in); `article` the number of the article of the law it touches, the first in the order of the law; `dossier` the label of the dossier it came through; the closest tie of all it has), `answers` (of a `Brief regering`: the motions and commitments it `ANSWERS`), `answered_by` (of a `toezegging`: the letters that fulfil it), `replaces` (of a changed `Motie` or `Amendement`: the paper it replaces, `REVISES`, "ter vervanging van nr. 19"), each such paper or commitment `{id, kind, title, date, number, dossier, surname, path}` (`kind` its `Document.Soort` or `toezegging`, `number` its nr. or the number of the commitment, `dossier` the label of its own dossier, `surname` its first signatory), at most twenty; `amends_articles` (of an `Amendement`: the articles it proposes to change, add or repeal, `effect` `amends`/`introduces`/`repeals`, in the order of their law, at most twenty) and `cites` (of an `uitspraak`: the articles it cites, the most mentioned first, at most five), each article `{key, bwb_id, number, law, law_short, effect, path}`; empty or null for the other kinds

get.description:
Basic service descriptor used by deployments: ``{"name": "lawgraph-api",
"version": ...}``.

Health check — verifies database connectivity; ``version`` the version of the API
(what a deploy checks against its tag). ``warm``: the answers every visitor
asks are computed for the data as it is now (null when the API does not warm up); a
deploy waits for true before its smoke test. ``warm_version`` the data version they
were last computed for (the answers a request gets while a newer one computes, null
before the first warm-up), ``data_version`` the version now, ``computing`` whether a
warm-up or an answer of a newer version is being computed. ``pools``: per connection
pool its size, the free connections and the reads waiting for one; ``busy`` what the
threads of the shared pools and of the background (the cache, the warm-up) run now,
and how long.

503 when the database is unreachable. ``warm`` is ``false`` while the warm-up runs,
also again after a data change; with ``LAWGRAPH_API_WARM_UP=false`` it is null and so
are ``warm_version``, ``data_version`` and ``computing``. ``pools`` has ``requests``
and ``background`` (null until it is first needed); ``busy`` names a computation of
the cache by its kind alone (``cache: <kind>``, never what was asked) and a part of
the warm-up as ``warm-up: <part>``, longest first. ``pools`` and ``busy`` are read
from memory.

DocumentTextResponse.title: DocumentTextResponse
DocumentTextResponse.description:
One document with its text.

``text`` is null until ``normalize tk-content`` has run for it: a paper
from before December 1994 has no XML and never gets one. ``sections`` are
the headings of the paper in document order, empty when there is no text or
the structure of the paper could not be read; their offsets are into
``text``. ``submitters`` are who submitted a motie or amendement, the indiener
first (empty for any other paper). ``dossier_numbers`` are the dossiers the
document is PART_OF, in either chamber; ``case_kinds`` the ``Zaak.Soort`` of the
cases it belongs to (Tweede Kamer only); ``explains`` are the articles and
instruments it explains, without duplicates.

DossierInstrumentDTO.title: DossierInstrumentDTO
DossierInstrumentDTO.description:
An instrument a dossier is tied to, once, and every way it is.

``links`` holds each ``relation`` (``legislated_in``: the instrument came out of this
dossier; ``establishes``: a publication legislated in it enacted the regulation;
``amends``, ``introduces``, ``repeals``: the dossier changes it, resolved from
the article or instrument that is changed to the parent instrument) with its
``status`` (``canoniek`` for what an amending publication enacted, ``voorgesteld`` for
what a bill of the dossier proposes). ``relation`` and ``status`` are the first link:
the enacted one before the proposed.

DossierRelationDTO.title: DossierRelationDTO
DossierRelationDTO.description:
A relation between this dossier and another, and which way it points.

* ``revises``: a supplementary budget or a slotwet revises the budget of its chapter
  and year; ``rule`` says which (``begrotingswijziging`` or ``slotwet``).
* ``accompanies``: a budget change is submitted with the ``nota`` its title names
  (``voorjaarsnota``, ``najaarsnota``, ``miljoenennota``).
* ``related_to``: the Kamer relates a case of the one dossier to a case of the other
  (``Zaak.GerelateerdNaar``), mostly a letter of the government to the motion it
  answers. ``cases`` counts the pairs of cases, ``case_kinds`` names their kinds
  (``Brief regering → Motie``).
* ``second_reading_of``: a change in the Grondwet in its second reading and the dossier of
  its first reading, whose papers explain it: the memorandum of 35785 only refers to those
  of 35418 and 35419.

``outgoing`` means this dossier is the subject: 37035-XXII revises 36800-XXII and
accompanies 37020. On 36800-XXII the same ``revises`` is ``incoming``.
